rationale:
Evidence: all 300 development trials so far ended off_track with no finishes. The best design is iteration 7 (score 125.3): 12 mm footprints, five sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02 (10 mm spacing), y = 0.03, kp 3.0, ki 0.4, kd 0.35, base_speed 1.3, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12. Max_error sits at 0.060 to 0.066 on almost every design, with 1 to 2 line-loss events per run. The robot loses the tape in bends, drifts past the 0.06 m limit, and the last_direction search cannot recover. Changes that did not help: widening the span alone (iteration 5), kd 0.45 (jitter, iteration 6), kp 3.5 with a narrower track (iteration 8), and a 16 mm footprint (iteration 9, 84.4). Iteration 3 showed that lower speed together with higher ki reduced drift slightly.

Change (one variable, relative to iteration 7): base_speed 1.3 to 1.15. Centrifugal drift scales with speed squared, so a slower entry into bends should keep the robot inside the 0.06 m band and reduce the line losses. Sensors, weights, kp, ki, kd, mass, track and line_loss are all held at iteration 7 values, so any change in result comes from speed.

Expected result: line_loss_events at 1 or fewer on oval and s-bend, max_error below 0.06 on oval, and a small progress cost. Hypotheses: H1, the line loss at bends is speed-driven drift, so lower speed reduces off-track ends. H2, progress falls only modestly, since the robot is off track before finishing anyway. Measurements needed: max_error and line_loss_events per track, progress on oval and s-bend, and steering_oscillation. If the robot now holds the line but progress is too low, raise base_speed toward 1.4. If max_error still reaches 0.06 with no line loss, raise kp before adding kd.
